`README.md`:

```md
# Deep Hack Brief

An auto-publishing site of daily deep technical reports on reverse engineering, anti-cheat internals, game modding, exploits and hacking in the era of AI: **daily report → Hugo → GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages**.

Live: `https://t-el.github.io/deephack-brief/`

Every day a new report lands in `content/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` on `main`, with commit message `report: YYYY-MM-DD`. That push triggers `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which builds with Hugo and deploys to GitHub Pages.

```
Report writer ──commit content/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md──▶ main ──▶ GitHub Actions (hugo --minify) ──▶ GitHub Pages
```

## What's in the repo

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `hugo.toml` | Site config: name, SEO, menus, palette defaults, monetization settings (empty = hidden on the public site). |
| `docs/report-style.md` | **The report spec**: front matter, section order, sourcing rules, safety line, checklist. |
| `content/reports/` | Daily reports. `2026-11-27.md` is the reference sample. Permalinks: `/reports/YYYY/MM/DD/`. |
| `content/about/`, `content/advertise.md` | About page and Advertise page (mailto `elkarroumytaha@gmail.com`). |
| `scripts/publish-report.sh` | Validates a report (front matter + required sections), build-checks it, commits and pushes. |
| `layouts/_partials/get_cover.html`, `get_cover_base.html`, `cover.html`, `templates/` | Auto-generated cover images and Open Graph / Twitter share tags. |
| `layouts/_partials/extend_head.html`, `extend_post_content.html` | Money blocks (AdSense, newsletter, sponsor, affiliates), rendered only when configured. |
| `layouts/_partials/social_icons.html`, `footer.html` | Subpath-safe RSS icon; footer without personal links. |
| `assets/css/extended/theme.css` | Terminal-green palette (dark default, light supported). |
| `assets/images/cover-base.png.b64` | Branded 1200×630 cover base, stored base64 and decoded by Hugo at build time. |
| `assets/fonts/*.ttf.b64` | IBM Plex Mono (SIL OFL, see `OFL.txt`), Latin subset, base64, decoded at build to paint title + date on covers. |
| `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` | Build and deploy to Pages on every push to `main`. PaperMod is checked out pinned to commit `118119693d8b5ac211b939775678310973bcb232` (no submodule; `themes/` is gitignored). |

Why base64 assets: the repo is managed through the GitHub API (text files only), so binary images and fonts are stored as `.b64` and decoded with `resources.FromString … encoding.Base64Decode` during the build. To change the cover, edit a PNG locally and run `base64 -w0 cover-base.png > assets/images/cover-base.png.b64`.

Built in: RSS (`/deephack-brief/index.xml`, plus `/reports/index.xml` and per-tag feeds), `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, tags, archive, search, reading time, share buttons.

## Cover images

Every report gets a cover (and matching `og:image` / `twitter:image`) automatically: Hugo paints the title and date onto the cover base. To use a custom image, put it under `static/images/` or `assets/images/` and set (no leading slash, so the `/deephack-brief/` subpath stays intact):

```yaml
cover:
  image: "images/my-cover.png"
  alt: "Short description"
```

## Setup

1. Repo: `t-el/deephack-brief` (public).
2. **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions.**
3. Actions → "Deploy Hugo site to GitHub Pages" → run (or push any commit). `baseURL` is injected by `actions/configure-pages`.

Daily writer: a scheduled Grok Bot routine researches the last 24–72 h, writes the report per `docs/report-style.md`, and commits `content/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with message `report: YYYY-MM-DD`. Locally you can use:

```bash
scripts/publish-report.sh /path/to/draft.md            # date defaults to today (Africa/Casablanca)
NO_PUSH=1 scripts/publish-report.sh draft.md           # commit only
```

### Local development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod themes/PaperMod
(cd themes/PaperMod && git checkout 118119693d8b5ac211b939775678310973bcb232)
hugo server -D          # http://localhost:1313
```

## Monetization notes

Settings live in `[params.monetization]` in `hugo.toml`. A block renders only when its fields are filled in; empty means nothing appears on the public site.

1. **Newsletter**: set `newsletterAction` (Beehiiv, Buttondown, ConvertKit, MailerLite form action) and optionally `newsletterCTA`.
2. **Sponsors**: set `sponsorText` + `sponsorURL`. Good fits for this audience: RE tool vendors, security training, CTFs/conferences, game-security hiring. The `/advertise/` page is always public.
3. **Affiliates**: add `[[params.monetization.affiliates]]` entries (`name`, `url`, `blurb`); rendered with `rel="sponsored"` and a disclosure.
4. **AdSense**: after ~20–30 quality posts, set both `adsenseClient` and `adsenseSlotInArticle`. Note: ad networks can be strict about "hacking" content; the defensive framing in the style guide matters.

## Content policy

Defensive and educational only: analysis, techniques at the level of public write-ups, and links to public research. No working cheats, no piracy links, no weaponized exploit code. See `docs/report-style.md` §6.

`content/about/index.md`:

```md
---
title: "About Deep Hack Brief"
description: "What this site covers, how the daily reports are made, and the ground rules."
ShowToc: false
hideMeta: true
hiddenInRss: true
---

**Deep Hack Brief** publishes one deep technical report every day on reverse engineering, game modding and hacking in the era of AI.

**What we cover**

- Anti-cheat internals: kernel drivers, EAC, BattlEye, Vanguard, ACE, and the BYOVD (bring your own vulnerable driver) problem they create.
- Game engine internals and modding toolchains: Unreal and Unity IL2CPP, static recompilation, decompilation projects, Frida, Cheat Engine, x64dbg, IDA, Ghidra and Binary Ninja.
- The emulation and console scene, at the research level.
- Malware reverse engineering, CVEs, exploit write-ups and fuzzing.
- AI x RE: LLM decompilation, MCP-driven Ghidra and IDA agents, and bugs found by AI.

**How it's made**

Each report is researched from primary sources (researcher blogs, advisories, papers, conference talks and code), then written up with the technical detail those sources support: structures, call flows, offsets and pseudocode-level explanations. Every claim links to its source.

**Ground rules**

This site is defensive and educational. We explain how things work and link to public research. We don't publish working cheats, piracy links or weaponized exploit code, and we don't link to them.

Want to sponsor a report or advertise? See [Advertise]({{< relref "advertise.md" >}}).

```

`content/reports/2026-11-27.md`:

```md
---
title: "Deep Hack Brief — Nov 27, 2026: One-bit .NET code-integrity bypass, Rust loader hides in game cheats, AI agents hunt Windows kernel 0-days"
date: 2026-11-27T08:00:00+00:00
lastmod: 2026-11-27T08:00:00+00:00
description: "Project Zero's .NET FlatImageLayout bypass of VirtualBox hardening and UMCI, WarpLoader/NWHStealer in fake FiveM cheats, DeepBinary's 146 kernel 0-days and MiCollab."
summary: "James Forshaw's one-bit .NET loader bypass, a Rust loader shipped inside fake game cheats, a community teardown of MTA's FairplayKD.sys, and frontier agents finding 146 Windows kernel 0-days."
tags: ["Project Zero", "Windows Internals", "Code Integrity", "Malware Analysis", "Game Security", "Anti-Cheat", "BYOVD", "AI x RE", "CVE", "Static Recompilation"]
categories: ["Daily Report"]
keywords: ["CVE-2026-87268", "CVE-2026-108398", "FlatImageLayout UMCI bypass", "WarpLoader NWHStealer", "FairplayKD.sys IOCTL 0x22E008", "DeepBinary benchmark"]
ShowToc: true
TocOpen: false
draft: false
---

## TL;DR

- **Project Zero (James Forshaw)** showed that .NET Framework 4's loader falls back to a data-only "flat" mapping when `NtCreateSection(SEC_IMAGE)` fails with `STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT`, which bypassed VirtualBox process hardening (**CVE-2026-87268**) and, through a wrong WLDP check, Windows UMCI (**CVE-2026-108398**, fixed in October).
- **InvokeRE researchers** traced fake FiveM, Valorant and Fortnite cheats on GitLab/GitHub to a Rust loader they call **WarpLoader**, which uses module stomping in `d3d10warp.dll`, a patchless hardware-breakpoint ETW bypass and indirect syscalls to inject **NWHStealer** into browsers.
- A community write-up of **FairplayKD.sys**, Multi Theft Auto's kernel anti-cheat driver, reconstructs one IOCTL (`0x22E008`) with about 20 subcommands, including arbitrary kernel read and write, which makes it BYOVD material.
- **DeepBinary** (UIUC) let frontier agents loose on 12 Windows kernel drivers with a disassembler and kernel debugger: over 200 bugs, 146 distinct previously unknown, and IDA or Binary Ninja beat Ghidra by about a fifth.
- **Mitel MiCollab**: five pre-auth bugs were exploited as zero-days before the Nov 16 advisory, and Accenture saw attacker infrastructure talking to commercial AI APIs in lockstep with the exploit traffic. CISA added all five to KEV.

## Top stories

### 1. One bit, two CVEs: .NET's FlatImageLayout fallback defeats VirtualBox hardening and UMCI

**What happened.** On Nov 23, Google Project Zero's James Forshaw published a follow-up to his 2017 VirtualBox research. He found three new bypasses of VirtualBox's protected-process hardening on Windows plus a broken fix for a 2020 bug, and wrote up one in detail: CVE-2026-87268. Oracle fixed it in VirtualBox. The same .NET behaviour also bypassed Windows User Mode Code Integrity (UMCI); Microsoft treated it as a zero-day, CVE-2026-108398, because Forshaw had already presented it at 44CON, and fixed it in October 2026.

**How it works.** In CLR v4, `PEImageLayout::Map` first builds a `MappedImageLayout`, which calls `CreateFileMapping` with `SEC_IMAGE`. If that fails *specifically* with `ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT`, the runtime does not abort. It builds a `FlatImageLayout` instead: a plain `PAGE_READONLY` data mapping with no image section, then runs only `PEDecoder::CheckFormat`. For managed-only code, that's enough to execute. Per Forshaw's reconstruction:

```cpp
// CLR v4, simplified from the Project Zero post
PEImageLayout* PEImageLayout::Map(HANDLE file) {
  PEImageLayout* image = new MappedImageLayout(file);  // SEC_IMAGE section
  if (!image->Image)                                    // failed with BAD_EXE_FORMAT
    image = new FlatImageLayout(file);                  // data-only mapping, no image load
  if (image->Image && !PEDecoder::CheckFormat(image->Image))
    ThrowWin32(ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT);
  return image;
}
```

Anything that enforces policy on *image section creation* never sees a flat mapping. In VirtualBox, the `NtCreateSection` hook (`supR3HardenedMonitor_NtCreateSection`) only screens image or executable mappings, and `supR3HardenedScreenImageCalcStatus` maps `VERR_LDR_ARCH_MISMATCH` to `STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT`. An `AnyCPU` assembly is emitted as a PE32 (x86, machine `0x14C`) file that still has code, so on an x64 host the parser reports an architecture mismatch, the hook returns the "magic" status, and the CLR falls back to the flat path. Getting the CLR to load the assembly in the first place goes through COM registration in the user's own hive (HKCU), which the hardened process consults.

For built-in code integrity there's no hook to abuse, so Forshaw looked for a file edit that makes the kernel reject the image section while .NET still accepts the file. Clearing `IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE` in the COFF `Characteristics` does exactly that. A WLDP guard was supposed to block the flat path under lockdown, but it compared the policy against `WLDP_LOCKDOWN_CONFIG_CI` in a way that let the exact flag set Windows 11 S Mode returns (`DEFINED | CONFIG_CI | UMCIENFORCE`) through. The fix tests `WLDP_LOCKDOWN_IS_ENFORCE(policy)` instead. Forshaw notes Protected Process Light is still reachable, since PPL bypasses are outside MSRC's servicing criteria. Full PP isn't, because it needs page hashes that the .NET DLLs lack.

**Defender's view.** Update VirtualBox and apply the October .NET Framework fix. Enabling WDAC's *Dynamic Code Security* option also blocks this path, but it breaks `Assembly.Load(byte[])` for every app. Our suggestion: hunt for .NET COM registrations under `HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\...\InprocServer32` pointing at `mscoree.dll` with user-writable `CodeBase` paths, and for PE files whose COFF `Characteristics` lack `0x0002` but which carry a CLR header. The broader lesson for anti-cheat and EDR authors: if a loader has a non-image fallback, image-load callbacks are not a complete view.

**Sources:** [Project Zero](https://projectzero.google/2026/11/virtualbox-process-hardening.html) · [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/google-researcher-shows-how-single-bit.html)

### 2. Fake FiveM and Valorant cheats ship a Rust loader with patchless ETW bypass and indirect syscalls

**What happened.** On Nov 23, Joshua Reynolds and Adam Krogsoe published an analysis of six downloaders found in fake game-cheat projects on GitLab and GitHub. The lures included "FiveM External Cheat", fake Valorant and Fortnite cheats, Lua executors (Xeno, Synapse X, Fluxus, Solara), an HWID spoofer and a FiveM graphics mod archive. All of them lead to a Rust loader the researchers track as WarpLoader, which delivers NWHStealer.

**How it works.** The first stage is crude. .NET downloaders host PowerShell through `System.Management.Automation` runspaces, add a Defender exclusion, drop into a GUID directory under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, and relaunch with `Verb = "runas"`. Go variants pull URLs from Pastebin dead drops, and one uses a Telegram page as a dead drop to a Pastebin. WarpLoader is where the craft is:

1. **Decrypt.** An embedded PE is decrypted with AES-256-CTR (key and IV hard-coded and published in the report).
2. **Anti-hook check.** It walks `InLoadOrderModuleList`, resolves `ntdll` and `kernel32` exports by DJB2 hash (e.g. `NtTraceControl` = `0x7EB77B17`), and checks for clean stubs (`4C 8B D1 B8`: `mov r10, rcx; mov eax, imm32`) and `0F 05 C3` (`syscall; ret`). If any stub is hooked, it calls `ExitProcess`.
3. **Patchless ETW bypass.** It registers a first-chance VEH and raises `INT 3`. The handler writes `NtTraceControl`'s address into `Dr0` and enables it in `Dr7`. On the resulting `EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP` it advances RIP by 3 bytes, past `mov r10, rcx`, which breaks the register setup for that syscall. No bytes are patched.
4. **Module stomping.** It loads `C:\Windows\System32\d3d10warp.dll` with `DONT_RESOLVE_DLL_REFERENCES`, finds an executable section big enough for the payload, makes it writable, wipes it and manually maps the PE there (relocations, imports, TLS, protections, `NtFlushInstructionCache`).
5. **Indirect syscalls.** The stomped Rust injector sorts `Zw*` exports by address to derive SSNs, stores each stub's `syscall; ret` address, and dispatches through it. It uses `ZwAllocateVirtualMemory`, `ZwWriteVirtualMemory` and `ZwCreateThreadEx` to reflectively inject NWHStealer into Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Opera GX, Vivaldi and Chromium. Oddly, it also byte-patches `EtwEventWrite`.

The stealer handles both legacy DPAPI `encrypted_key` and Chromium's app-bound `app_bound_encrypted_key`. For the latter it calls each browser's Elevation Service (`IElevator` / `IElevator2` interfaces, CLSIDs reconstructed in the report) from inside the injected browser process. It uploads records with AES-256-CBC, using a key derived by SHA-256 from an XOR-encoded secret.

**Defender's view.** The downloaders are noisy: PowerShell `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath`, `runas` relaunches, and scheduled tasks named `WindowsUpdateService` or `SystemBackgroundUpdate`. Higher-signal behaviour for EDR: a non-image-backed or modified `.text` in `d3d10warp.dll`, hardware breakpoints set on `ntdll` syscall stubs, and remote threads created in browsers. IOCs and rules are on the authors' GitHub. For game communities: "external cheats" and "spoofers" are a reliable malware vector. That's a security finding, not a moral one.

**Sources:** [InvokeRE](https://invokere.com/posts/2026/11/from-game-cheats-to-nwhstealer-following-a-rust-loader-infection-chain/)

### 3. FairplayKD.sys teardown: an old anti-cheat driver that exposes kernel R/W

**What happened.** A write-up on the romdump forum this week reconstructs FairplayKD.sys, the x64 kernel component of Multi Theft Auto: San Andreas' "Fairplay" anti-cheat (build tag `fairplay_7`). It's dropped to `C:\ProgramData\MTA San Andreas All\Common\temp\` and driven by `netc.dll`. The author says the analysis is static and lists about a dozen unresolved inconsistencies. Treat it as a community write-up that hasn't been independently verified.

**How it works.** According to the write-up, the driver exposes a single device IOCTL, `0x22E008`, with roughly 20 subcommands chosen by a field in the input buffer. A version handshake returns `363` (`0x16B`). The subcommands include copying from an arbitrary kernel address (`0x78`), writing to one (`0x7C`), `ntoskrnl` base and export disclosure (`0x79`), resolving a caller-supplied routine name through `MmGetSystemRoutineAddress` (`0x7A`), process tagging used by its tracking model (`0x82`/`0x83`), and system enumeration through AuxKlib or `ZwQuerySystemInformation` (`0x84`). It also has process and thread open, read and write, plus a write-then-resume thread primitive. Strings are hidden with a 7-bit XOR/subtract cipher, and APIs are resolved at runtime. The author stresses that the IOCTL "magic + checksum" is protocol validation anyone holding the client DLL can reproduce, not caller authentication, and that the device's security descriptor hasn't been recovered. The signing certificate is an individual developer cert that expired in 2018. The write-up records the driver as loading with HVCI enabled.

**Defender's view.** This is the same story as August's XIGNCODE3 `xhunter1.sys` LPE (CVE-2026-3609) and the ACE-BASE physical-memory research: a signed anti-cheat driver with a generic R/W interface is a BYOVD primitive for whoever finds it on disk. Defenders should block it by hash or signer through WDAC or ASR's vulnerable-signed-driver rule, and watch for `FairplayKD.sys` loads outside MTA sessions. Anti-cheat vendors should take the hint: never expose raw R/W, authenticate the caller (process protection, signed caller checks), and lock down the device DACL.

**Sources:** [romdump: FairplayKD.sys write-up](https://romdump.net/t/3) · context: [BlackSnufkin on xhunter1.sys](https://blacksnufkin.github.io/posts/Hunting-the-Hunter/) · [afflicted.sh on ACE-BASE.sys](https://www.afflicted.sh/blog/posts/ace-fullhouse.html)

### 4. Static recompilation keeps eating game preservation, and Rockstar pushes back

**What happened.** Emu Radar's Nov 25 roundup reports that the "Leonida" GTA 6 static-recompilation project went offline on Nov 23–24 after Rockstar pulled its Discord server of more than 179,000 members. The project followed leaked Xbox build files. The same roundup covers several shipping recomp projects: AlolaHawaiCpp v0.1.0-alpha (3DS Pokémon Sun/Moon/Ultra), BlueStingerRecomp v0.9.7-8 (Dreamcast SH-4 to C++20), and "Silent Hill PC" v1.0.0, a C++20 engine built against the Silent Hill decompilation project. Its developer says it was written with Claude Opus 5.5 and GLM 5.2.

**How it works.** Static recompilation lifts guest machine code ahead of time into host source or IR instead of interpreting or JIT-ing it at runtime. AlolaHawaiCpp reportedly runs about 98–99% of the ARM11 code natively and leans on a modified Azahar core for the rest, which is likely the usual hybrid fallback for indirect branches and code that static lifting can't resolve (our inference; the roundup doesn't say). BlueStingerRecomp is verified against the Flycast emulator. These projects need the user's own disc dump and don't ship game data.

**Defender's view.** No working GTA 6 PC build exists, so any "GTA 6 PC" executable is malware, as Emu Radar warns. That's the same lure economics as story 2. The legal line is the input: recomp of owned dumps is preservation work; anything built on leaked proprietary builds draws takedowns.

**Sources:** [Emu Radar roundup](https://emu-radar.customfw.xyz/news/roundup-2026-11-25/)

## Tooling and releases

- **Frida 17.27.6** (Nov 25): embedded builds now extract helpers into shared per-build resource directories, verified by SHA-256 and reclaimed after crashes. On macOS arm64, code patching remaps a patched copy over each run of pages atomically, with no thread suspension and no window where pages aren't executable, which fixes attach/detach crashes in GCD-heavy processes. Local sessions get the agent through an unlinked shared memory object, so `frida-agent.dylib` no longer touches disk. [Release notes](https://frida.re/news/2026/11/25/frida-17-27-6-released/)
- **IDA 9.5 UEFI support** (Hex-Rays deep dive, Nov 17): a UEFITool-based loader opens a whole SPI dump or capsule into one database, types `gBS`, `gRT` and `gSmst`, and resolves protocol GUIDs. The decompiler output reads close to EDK2 source. It's one address size per database, so IA32 PEI modules need the 32-bit load format. About 9 minutes for 400+ DXE/SMM modules on an M4. [Hex-Rays](https://hex-rays.com/blog/introducing-native-uefi-firmware-support-in-ida-9.5)
- **IDA 9.5** (Oct 26) for context: new Dalvik, TriCore and Hexagon decompilers, FLIRT 2.0, an official **IDA MCP** server (Hex-Rays claims about 20% fewer tokens than typical IDA MCP implementations), and **IDA Pro Headless** licensing aimed at agent fleets. [Hex-Rays](https://hex-rays.com/blog/ida-9.5-release)
- **Current stable baselines**: Ghidra 12.2 (Oct 22) and Binary Ninja 6.0 R2 / build 6.0.10905 (Oct 20; PE/ELF loader hardening, RTTI analysis hang fix, Ghidra-export fixes). [Ghidra releases](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases) · [Binary Ninja](https://binary.ninja/2026/10/20/6.0-release-2.html)

## CVE and exploit corner

- **CVE-2026-133275, -133303, -133311, -133323, -133324 (Mitel MiCollab ≤ 10.3.0.18)**: unauthenticated file upload, XML injection, unauthorized access, command injection and auth bypass in the audio, web and video conferencing (AWV) component. Accenture Apex Labs found a web shell dated Nov 15, a day before Mitel's Nov 16 advisory, with commands running 12 minutes after the first request and root within about 30 minutes. CISA added all five to KEV on Nov 25, with federal deadlines of Nov 28 (four bugs) and Dec 9 (one). [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/mitel-micollab-zero-days-exploited-in-suspected-ai-assisted-attacks/) · [Mitel MISA-2026-0012](https://www.mitel.com/support/security-advisories/mitel-product-security-advisory-misa-2026-0012) · [CISA](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/11/25/cisa-adds-10-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog)
- **CVE-2026-87268 (VirtualBox) / CVE-2026-108398 (.NET Framework 4)**: see story 1. The bug class is policy enforced at section creation while the loader has a non-section fallback path.
- **CVE-2026-3609 (XIGNCODE3 `xhunter1.sys` ≤ 2023.12.7.78)**, background for story 3: CERT/CC widened the affected range in August after BlackSnufkin showed the current production driver, WHQL-signed and loading under HVCI with the Microsoft blocklist enabled, still gives a standard user SYSTEM. Wellbia re-signs it per title, so hash blocklists need the whole catalogue. [BlackSnufkin](https://blacksnufkin.github.io/posts/Hunting-the-Hunter/)

## AI x RE

**DeepBinary: frontier agents vs. Windows kernel binaries.** A UIUC team (arXiv 2611.33486) gave agents only a target binary, a disassembler server and a kernel debugger on network-isolated VM pairs. The targets were 12 inbox drivers on Windows 11 build 26100.7462, including `ntfs.sys`, `refs.sys`, `clfs.sys`, `cldflt.sys`, `vhdmp.sys`, `win32k*`, `clipsp.sys`, `HTTP.sys`, `tcpip.sys` and `afd.sys`. Every report needs a crashing PoC, which a judge replays on fresh VMs. Across 204 campaigns, 4,119 agent-hours and $53.5K in tokens, seven models across three coding agents (including Codex and Claude Code) found bugs in all 12 targets. That's over 200 vulnerabilities, 146 distinct defects whose PoCs still crash a Windows build released nine months later, and an estimated $661K in bounty value. GPT-6 Sol in Codex was the top configuration, with 116 unique bugs in the paper's table. The methodology findings matter most for practitioners. Removing the disassembler server cut Sol's unique bugs by 67%, and the median time to first report rose from 160K to 651K output tokens. Stripping symbols cut them by 37%. IDA Pro or Binary Ninja yielded about a fifth more bugs than Ghidra. Caveats: impact is estimated by an LLM judge, and only 16 of the 70 RQ1 defects were found by more than one model, so coverage is far from saturated. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33486)

**Agentic offense is now routine telemetry.** Microsoft (Nov 25) says state and criminal actors, including Salt Typhoon, Onyx Sleet and Storm-0940, have adopted ARTEX, a public AI pentest framework released in July. It uses no novel techniques; Microsoft calls its machine-speed retry and variation pattern the most durable detection signal. Amazon (via Ars Technica, Nov 24) described agents on the open-source Cairn framework finding a path-traversal zero-day in a medical-imaging AI app. In about 11 minutes they went from API mapping to arbitrary file write, then got root by writing `sitecustomize.py` and triggering a training endpoint that spawned a fresh Python interpreter. In the MiCollab case above, Accenture saw attacker traffic to AI APIs resume in the same second as an auth-bypass request. That's suggestive, not proof of how the AI was used. [Microsoft Security](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/25/what-defenders-need-to-know-artex-agentic-ai-framework-threat-actors-abuse/) · [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/amazon-says-hackers-ai-agents-found-and-exploited-0-day-with-little-human-input/)

**Patch diff to exploit.** CyberBinGym (arXiv 2611.10723) hands agents stripped vulnerable and patched binaries for 100 real bugs across 53 projects. The best agent recovered the bug in 88% of tasks but exploited only 20%, and having the patched binary raised its exploit rate from 10% to 25% on a matched subset. That's the n-day window shrinking in numbers. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10723)

## Reading list

- **Tirith: "You Shall Not Pass into Ring-0!" (CCS '26, published Nov 14)**: runs games in protected VMs with a mutually trusted virtualization monitor, a library OS and a graphics-sharing pipeline, instead of an untrusted ring-0 anti-cheat. It's the strongest academic answer yet to the BYOVD problem in stories 1 and 3. [ACM DL](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3830454.3846577)
- **"full house beats ACE" (afflicted.sh, Aug 20)**: dumping Tencent ACE's VMProtect'd drivers from kernel memory using only third-party WHQL drivers, then arguing that the CVE-2024-22830 fix is mostly decorative. A masterclass in BYOVD chaining and patch analysis. [afflicted.sh](https://www.afflicted.sh/blog/posts/ace-fullhouse.html)
- **"Hunting the Hunter" (BlackSnufkin, Aug 4)**: a full root-cause walk of the XIGNCODE3 `xhunter1.sys` LPE and why signing plus blocklists failed. [BlackSnufkin](https://blacksnufkin.github.io/posts/Hunting-the-Hunter/)
- **Project Zero, "Policy and Disclosure: 2026 Edition" (Nov 13)**: the new disclosure policy that will shape when write-ups like story 1 land. [Project Zero](https://projectzero.google/2026/11/disclosure-policy.html)

`docs/report-style.md`:

```md
# Deep Hack Brief: Report Style Guide

The spec every daily report follows. If it isn't in this file, it isn't part of the format. Reference example: `content/reports/2026-11-27.md`.

Audience: reverse engineers, exploit developers, anti-cheat and game-security engineers, malware analysts, emulator and modding devs. Assume they know what an IOCTL, a vtable, IL2CPP metadata or a syscall stub is. Don't explain basics; explain mechanisms.

## 1. File

- Path: `content/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (date in **Africa/Casablanca**, the morning of publication).
- One report per day. If the file already exists, update it rather than creating a second one.
- UTF-8, LF line endings, **no raw HTML** (Goldmark `unsafe = false` strips it). Use fenced code blocks with a language tag (`c`, `cpp`, `asm`, `text`, `python`, `csharp`).

## 2. Front matter (YAML, exact keys)

```yaml
---
title: "Deep Hack Brief — Nov 27, 2026: <2–3 biggest stories, ≤ 110 chars after the colon>"
date: 2026-11-27T08:00:00+00:00        # ISO 8601 with offset, never in the future at build time
lastmod: 2026-11-27T08:00:00+00:00
description: "<140–160 char SEO summary naming the top 3–4 stories>"
summary: "<1 sentence, ≤ 200 chars, shown on list pages>"
tags: ["Anti-Cheat", "Windows Kernel", "Ghidra"]   # 5–10, reuse existing tags, Title Case
categories: ["Daily Report"]                       # always exactly this
keywords: ["<3–6 search phrases, e.g. CVE ids, driver names, tool versions>"]
ShowToc: true
TocOpen: false
draft: false
---
```

Quote every string. No trailing commas. No `cover:` key needed: a cover image is generated from the title and date at build time.

Suggested tag vocabulary: `Anti-Cheat`, `BYOVD`, `Windows Kernel`, `Game Modding`, `Static Recompilation`, `Emulation`, `Console Scene`, `Unreal Engine`, `Unity IL2CPP`, `Frida`, `IDA Pro`, `Ghidra`, `Binary Ninja`, `x64dbg`, `Cheat Engine`, `Malware Analysis`, `Exploit Analysis`, `CVE`, `Fuzzing`, `Firmware`, `AI Security`, `AI x RE`, `MCP`, `Project Zero`.

## 3. Body: section order (H2 headings, exact text)

1. `## TL;DR`: 4–6 bullets, one per item, **bold the actor/artifact**, one sentence each with the key technical fact (CVE id, driver name, version, primitive).
2. `## Top stories`: 3–5 stories ranked by technical significance. Each story:
   ```markdown
   ### N. <Plain technical headline>

   **What happened.** 2–4 sentences: who, what, when, affected versions, fix status.

   **How it works.** The technical deep dive, 150–400 words. Go as low as the public research goes:
   structures and offsets, IOCTL codes and input layouts, call flows (A → B → C), flags and status codes,
   and pseudocode-level explanation in a short fenced block (paraphrased or quoted with attribution, ≤ 15 lines).
   Mark inferences as inferences.

   **Defender's view.** 2–4 sentences: detection opportunities, mitigations, what to patch or block, open questions.

   **Sources:** [Researcher/Publisher](url) · [Advisory/Code](url)
   ```
3. `## Tooling and releases`: 2–6 bullets on RE / modding / emulation tool releases (IDA, Ghidra, Binary Ninja, Frida, x64dbg, Cheat Engine, dnSpyEx, Il2CppDumper, UE4SS, emulators, recomp toolchains). Version number, what changed that matters technically, link to release notes.
4. `## CVE and exploit corner`: 2–5 bullets: CVE id, product and versions, bug class, exploited-in-the-wild status (cite CISA KEV or vendor), patch. Root cause in one sentence when known.
5. `## AI x RE`: 1–3 items on AI-assisted reverse engineering and vulnerability research: LLM decompilation, MCP-driven Ghidra/IDA/Binary Ninja agents, benchmarks, AI-found bugs, agentic offensive tooling seen in the wild. Give numbers and methodology, and say what is and isn't proven.
6. `## Reading list`: 3–6 bullets of worthwhile deeper material (papers, talks, long write-ups), each with one line on why to read it. Older items allowed here.
7. `## Sources`: full list, `- Publisher — [Title](url) (Mon D, YYYY)`.
8. Closing italic line: `*Defensive and educational analysis of public research. No working cheats, piracy links or weaponized exploit code. Drafted with AI assistance from the sources above and reviewed for accuracy.*`

Length: 1,800–3,000 words. Dense beats long.

## 4. Story selection

- News from the **last 24–72 hours** (this is a niche with a slower news cycle than mainstream tech). Older items only as context or in the Reading list.
- Priority: new technical write-ups with root cause (Project Zero, researcher blogs, conference talks) > anti-cheat / kernel driver research > in-the-wild exploitation with technical detail > AI x RE results with real methodology > major tool releases > console/emulation/recomp milestones > game-modding scene news.
- Mix: at least one anti-cheat or game-security item and one AI x RE item per report when the news allows. Don't run more than 2 items from the same researcher or vendor.
- Skip: rumor without a primary source, cheat sellers' marketing, "undetected" claims, leaks of proprietary builds, drama.

## 5. Sourcing rules

Cite **primary sources first**, and every story needs at least one:

- Researcher blogs and write-ups (e.g. Project Zero, individual researcher sites, vendor research labs).
- Code and releases on GitHub/GitLab (README, release notes, commits); link to the repo, never to a binary download.
- Papers (arXiv, USENIX, IEEE S&P, CCS, NDSS) and conference talks (Black Hat, DEF CON, REcon, OffensiveCon, 44CON, CCC).
- Vendor advisories, MSRC, CERT/CC, NVD, CISA KEV.
- Official tool release notes (Hex-Rays, Vector 35, NSA Ghidra, frida.re).

Secondary sources (allowed as support, never alone for technical claims): The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek, Ars Technica, The Record, Wccftech/TechPowerUp for scene news, r/ReverseEngineering and r/netsec threads (link the underlying write-up instead when there is one).

Community forums such as **UnknownCheats or similar scene boards: news-level only** (that a write-up or tool exists, what it claims). Never link cheat downloads, loaders, "undetected" offerings or paid cheat providers. Forum write-ups get a caveat ("community write-up, not independently verified").

Accuracy:

- Never invent numbers, offsets, IOCTL codes, CVE ids, quotes, dates or URLs. If it isn't in a source, leave it out.
- Attribute claims ("the researcher says…", "Accenture assesses…"). Separate confirmed facts from vendor marketing and from inference.
- Canonical URLs only (no tracking params, no AMP).

## 6. Safety line (non-negotiable)

- Explain techniques at the level of the public write-up; **don't add** working exploit chains, shellcode, bypass instructions, signature evasion steps or cheat code.
- Pseudocode illustrates root cause and must not be a drop-in PoC.
- No piracy: no links to ROMs, game dumps, leaked builds, FPKG/warez sources, or "how to pirate" guides. Scene news about jailbreaks and emulators is fine at the research/news level.
- No doxxing of researchers, cheat devs or players.

## 7. Voice

- Precise, terse, technical. Active voice. Use the correct term (e.g. "arbitrary kernel R/W primitive via METHOD_BUFFERED IOCTL", not "hacking the kernel").
- Neutral and skeptical: no hype ("insane", "game-changing"), no cheering for attackers.
- Explain why a mechanism matters to defenders and builders.

## 8. Publishing checklist

- [ ] Filename date = front matter date (Casablanca), date not in the future
- [ ] Section headings exactly as in §3
- [ ] Each top story has What happened / How it works / Defender's view / Sources
- [ ] Every claim sourced; no raw HTML; no binary, piracy or cheat links
- [ ] `hugo --minify` builds with no errors
- [ ] Commit message: `report: YYYY-MM-DD`, pushed to `main` (this triggers the Pages deploy)

```

    {{- $processableFormats := (slice "jpg" "jpeg" "png" "tif" "bmp" "gif" "webp") -}}

    {{- if $addLink }}
        <a href="{{ $imgdl }}" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
    {{- end }}

    {{- if $cover.resource -}}
        {{- $img := $cover.resource -}}
        {{- if (and (in $processableFormats $img.MediaType.SubType) $responsiveImages (eq $prod true)) }}
            <img loading="{{ $loading }}"
                srcset='{{- range $size := $sizes -}}
                            {{- if (ge $img.Width $size) }}
                                {{- printf "%s %s" (($img.Resize (printf "%sx" $size)).Permalink) (printf "%sw," $size) }}
                            {{- end }}
                        {{- end }}
                        {{- printf "%s %dw" ($img.Permalink) ($img.Width) }}'
                src="{{ $img.Permalink }}"
                sizes="(min-width: 768px) 720px, 100vw"
                width="{{ $img.Width }}" height="{{ $img.Height }}"
                alt="{{ $alt }}">
        {{- else }}
            <img loading="{{ $loading }}" src="{{ $imgdl }}" width="{{ $img.Width }}" height="{{ $img.Height }}" alt="{{ $alt }}">
        {{- end }}
    {{- else }}
        <img loading="{{ $loading }}" src="{{ $imgdl }}" alt="{{ $alt }}">
    {{- end }}

    {{- if $addLink }}
        </a>
    {{- end -}}

    {{- if $.IsSingle }}
        {{ with $cover.caption -}}
            <figcaption>{{ . | markdownify }}</figcaption>
        {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
</figure>
{{- end }}
{{- end -}}

    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"
        stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-chevrons-up">

    </svg>

<script>
    let menu = document.getElementById('menu');
    if (menu) {
        // Set the scroll position
        const scrollPosition = localStorage.getItem("menu-scroll-position");
        if (scrollPosition) {
            menu.scrollLeft = parseInt(scrollPosition, 10);
        }
        
        // Save once scrolling settles, not on every event
        let menuScrollTimeout;
        menu.addEventListener("scroll", function () {
            clearTimeout(menuScrollTimeout);
            menuScrollTimeout = setTimeout(function () {
                localStorage.setItem("menu-scroll-position", menu.scrollLeft);
            }, 150);
        }, { passive: true });
    }

    document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]').forEach(anchor => {
        anchor.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
            e.preventDefault();
            var id = this.getAttribute("href").substr(1);
            const target = document.querySelector(`[id='${decodeURIComponent(id)}']`);
            if (!window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
                target.scrollIntoView({
                    behavior: "smooth"
                });
            } else {
                target.scrollIntoView();
            }
            // Move keyboard focus to the target like native anchor navigation,
            // so the next Tab continues from there instead of from this link
            if (target.tabIndex < 0 && !target.hasAttribute("tabindex")) {
                target.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
            }
            target.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            if (id === "top") {
                history.replaceState(null, null, " ");
            } else {
                history.pushState(null, null, `#${id}`);
            }
        });
    });

</script>

{{- if (not site.Params.disableScrollToTop) }}
<script>
    var toplink = document.getElementById("top-link");
    var scrollTicking = false;
    // At most one check per frame
    window.addEventListener("scroll", function () {
        if (scrollTicking) {
            return;
        }
        scrollTicking = true;
        requestAnimationFrame(function () {
            const scrollThreshold = window.innerHeight;
            const shown = document.body.scrollTop > scrollThreshold || document.documentElement.scrollTop > scrollThreshold;
            toplink.classList.toggle("hidden", !shown);
            scrollTicking = false;
        });
    }, { passive: true });

</script>
{{- end }}

{{- if (not site.Params.disableThemeToggle) }}
<script>
    document.getElementById("theme-toggle").addEventListener("click", () => {
        const html = document.querySelector("html");
        if (html.dataset.theme === "dark") {
            html.dataset.theme = 'light';
            localStorage.setItem("pref-theme", 'light');
        } else {
            html.dataset.theme = 'dark';
            localStorage.setItem("pref-theme", 'dark');
        }
    })

</script>
{{- end }}

{{- if (and (eq .Kind "page") (ne .Layout "archives") (ne .Layout "search") (.Param "ShowCodeCopyButtons")) }}
<script>
    document.querySelectorAll('pre > code').forEach((codeblock) => {
        const container = codeblock.parentNode.parentNode;

        const copybutton = document.createElement('button');
        copybutton.classList.add('copy-code');
        copybutton.innerHTML = '{{- i18n "code_copy" | default "copy" }}';

        function copyingDone() {
            copybutton.innerHTML = '{{- i18n "code_copied" | default "copied!" }}';
            setTimeout(() => {
                copybutton.innerHTML = '{{- i18n "code_copy" | default "copy" }}';
            }, 2000);
        }

        copybutton.addEventListener('click', (cb) => {
            if ('clipboard' in navigator) {
                navigator.clipboard.writeText(codeblock.textContent);
                copyingDone();
                return;
            }

            const range = document.createRange();
            range.selectNodeContents(codeblock);
            const selection = window.getSelection();
            selection.removeAllRanges();
            selection.addRange(range);
            try {
                document.execCommand('copy');
                copyingDone();
            } catch (e) { };
            selection.removeRange(range);
        });

        if (container.classList.contains("highlight")) {
            container.appendChild(copybutton);
        } else if (container.parentNode.firstChild == container) {
            // td containing LineNos
        } else if (codeblock.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.nodeName == "TABLE") {
            // table containing LineNos and code
            codeblock.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.parentNode.appendChild(copybutton);
        } else {
            // code blocks not having highlight as parent class
            codeblock.parentNode.appendChild(copybutton);
        }
    });
</script>
{{- end }}

```

`layouts/_partials/get_cover.html`:

```html
{{- /*
  Resolve a report's heading image.

  If front matter sets cover.image, use that (page bundle, assets/, or static/,
  same lookup order as PaperMod). Otherwise, for reports, paint the title and
  date onto assets/images/cover-base.png at build time.

  Returns a map:
    has       bool
    resource  image resource when Hugo can process it, else false
    url       absolute URL (includes the /deephack-brief/ subpath)
    alt       alt text
    caption   optional caption (may contain markdown)
*/ -}}
{{- $page := . -}}
{{- $alt := $page.Title | plainify -}}
{{- $caption := "" -}}
{{- $resource := false -}}
{{- $url := "" -}}

{{- with $page.Params.cover }}
  {{- if .alt }}
    {{- $alt = .alt | plainify -}}
  {{- else if .caption }}
    {{- $alt = .caption | plainify -}}
  {{- end }}
  {{- with .caption }}{{ $caption = . }}{{ end }}
{{- end }}

{{- if $page.Params.cover.image }}
  {{- $img := $page.Params.cover.image -}}
  {{- $cover := ($page.Resources.ByType "image").GetMatch (printf "*%s*" $img) -}}
  {{- if not $cover }}
    {{- $cover = (resources.ByType "image").GetMatch (printf "*%s*" $img) -}}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if $cover }}
    {{- $resource = $cover -}}
    {{- $url = $cover.Permalink -}}
  {{- else if eq ($page.Params.cover.relative | default false) true }}
    {{- $url = (path.Join $page.RelPermalink $img) | absURL -}}
  {{- else }}
    {{- $url = $img | absURL -}}
  {{- end }}
{{- else if and $page.IsPage (eq $page.Section "reports") }}
  {{- $base := partial "get_cover_base.html" . -}}
  {{- $fontTitle := false -}}
  {{- $fontDate := false -}}
  {{- with resources.Get "fonts/IBMPlexMono-SemiBold.ttf.b64" }}
    {{- $fontTitle = resources.FromString "fonts/IBMPlexMono-SemiBold.ttf" (.Content | strings.TrimSpace | encoding.Base64Decode) -}}
  {{- end }}
  {{- with resources.Get "fonts/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf.b64" }}
    {{- $fontDate = resources.FromString "fonts/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf" (.Content | strings.TrimSpace | encoding.Base64Decode) -}}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if and $base $fontTitle $fontDate }}
    {{- $title := $page.Title | plainify -}}
    {{- $date := $page.Date.Format "January 2, 2006" -}}
    {{- $size := 48 -}}
    {{- $tlen := strings.RuneCount $title -}}
    {{- if gt $tlen 80 }}{{ $size = 40 }}{{ end }}
    {{- if gt $tlen 120 }}{{ $size = 36 }}{{ end }}
    {{- /* Wrap so the title keeps the same 72px padding on the right as on the left.
         images.Text wraps to the full image width and would run into the border. */ -}}
    {{- $pad := 72 -}}
    {{- $maxWidth := sub 1200 (mul $pad 2) -}}
    {{- $maxChars := math.Floor (div (float $maxWidth) (mul (float $size) 0.60)) | int -}}
    {{- $wrapped := "" -}}
    {{- $line := "" -}}
    {{- range (split $title " ") }}
      {{- $word := . -}}
      {{- $trial := $word -}}
      {{- if $line }}{{ $trial = printf "%s %s" $line $word }}{{ end }}
      {{- if gt (strings.RuneCount $trial) $maxChars }}
        {{- if $line }}
          {{- if $wrapped }}{{ $wrapped = printf "%s\n%s" $wrapped $line }}{{ else }}{{ $wrapped = $line }}{{ end }}
          {{- $line = $word -}}
        {{- else }}
          {{- if $wrapped }}{{ $wrapped = printf "%s\n%s" $wrapped $word }}{{ else }}{{ $wrapped = $word }}{{ end }}
          {{- $line = "" -}}
        {{- end }}
      {{- else }}
        {{- $line = $trial -}}
      {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
    {{- if $line }}
      {{- if $wrapped }}{{ $wrapped = printf "%s\n%s" $wrapped $line }}{{ else }}{{ $wrapped = $line }}{{ end }}
    {{- end }}
    {{- $ls := math.Round (mul (float $size) 0.22) | int -}}
    {{- $titleOpts := dict
      "color"       "#E6F2EA"
      "font"        $fontTitle
      "size"        $size
      "linespacing" $ls
      "alignx"      "left"
      "aligny"      "top"
      "x"           $pad
      "y"           200
    -}}
    {{- $dateOpts := dict
      "color"  "#39E58C"
      "font"   $fontDate
      "size"   22
      "alignx" "left"
      "aligny" "top"
      "x"      $pad
      "y"      548
    -}}
    {{- $generated := $base | images.Filter (images.Text $wrapped $titleOpts) (images.Text $date $dateOpts) -}}
    {{- $resource = $generated -}}
    {{- $url = $generated.Permalink -}}
  {{- end }}
{{- end }}

{{- return (dict "has" (ne $url "") "resource" $resource "url" $url "alt" $alt "caption" $caption) -}}

```

`scripts/publish-report.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish a daily report: copy it into content/reports/, build-check, commit, push to main.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/publish-report.sh path/to/report.md [YYYY-MM-DD]
#
# Date defaults to today in Africa/Casablanca. Env options:
#   NO_PUSH=1     commit locally but don't push
#   SKIP_BUILD=1  skip the `hugo --minify` check
#   REMOTE=origin BRANCH=main
set -euo pipefail

SRC="${1:?usage: $0 path/to/report.md [YYYY-MM-DD]}"
DATE="${2:-$(TZ=Africa/Casablanca date +%F)}"
REMOTE="${REMOTE:-origin}"
BRANCH="${BRANCH:-main}"

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

[[ -f "$SRC" ]] || { echo "error: $SRC not found" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ "$DATE" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ ]] || { echo "error: bad date '$DATE'" >&2; exit 1; }

# Basic format checks (see docs/report-style.md)
head -n1 "$SRC" | grep -qx -- '---' || { echo "error: missing YAML front matter" >&2; exit 1; }
for key in title date description tags categories; do
  grep -qE "^${key}:" "$SRC" || { echo "error: front matter missing '${key}'" >&2; exit 1; }
done
for h in '## TL;DR' '## Top stories' '## Tooling and releases' '## CVE and exploit corner' '## AI x RE' '## Reading list' '## Sources'; do
  grep -qF "$h" "$SRC" || { echo "error: missing section '$h'" >&2; exit 1; }
done
grep -qE '^draft:\s*true' "$SRC" && { echo "error: report is marked draft: true" >&2; exit 1; }

DEST="content/reports/${DATE}.md"
if [[ "$(realpath "$SRC")" != "$(realpath -m "$DEST")" ]]; then
  cp "$SRC" "$DEST"
fi

if [[ "${SKIP_BUILD:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
  command -v hugo >/dev/null || { echo "error: hugo not installed (or set SKIP_BUILD=1)" >&2; exit 1; }
  hugo --minify --quiet --destination "$(mktemp -d)" || { echo "error: hugo build failed" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

git add "$DEST"
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "nothing to commit: $DEST unchanged"; exit 0
fi
git commit -m "report: ${DATE}"

if [[ "${NO_PUSH:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
  echo "committed locally (NO_PUSH=1): $DEST"; exit 0
fi
git remote get-url "$REMOTE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: no git remote '$REMOTE' configured yet" >&2; exit 1; }
git pull --rebase "$REMOTE" "$BRANCH"
git push "$REMOTE" "HEAD:${BRANCH}"
echo "published: $DEST → ${REMOTE}/${BRANCH} (GitHub Actions will deploy)"

```
